blocks.text: Living in Stave Falls, Mission

Stave Falls, in the District of Mission, is a rural community at the north end of the municipality, around Stave Lake, Hayward Lake, and the Stave River. It is inside city limits, even though the streets feel country. The Stave Falls Generating Station, a BC Hydro site, is a local landmark. Shoreline around the lakes is part of a hydroelectric reservoir, so water levels, access, and tenure should be confirmed with BC Hydro and the District.

Homes for sale in Stave Falls are mainly acreages, forested lots, and country houses, including properties with a view of the lakes. Recreation gathers around Hayward Lake and the dam area, with trails and day-use sites rather than a town shopping street. Everyday errands are a drive south toward Steelhead and the urban core of Mission.

Transit is limited; most trips are by car. Nearby public schools include Stave Falls Elementary. Middle and secondary students often attend schools in urban Mission. Check the SD75 school locator. Confirm well and septic or municipal servicing, reservoir setbacks, and rural zoning with the District before you plan a new dwelling.

Stave Falls is inside the City of Mission, unlike Dewdney-Deroche and Lake Errock, which are in the regional district. The City's Rural Mission Strategy names Stave Falls first among the rural communities it covers ("From Stave Falls, Steelhead and Silverdale to our other rural neighbourhoods") and ties that work to the City's Official Community Plan. items.t: This page covers the Stave Falls community in the northern part of the City of Mission, around Stave Lake, Hayward Lake and the Stave River. Listings here show the "Stave Falls" area and a Mission mailing address (postal codes starting V4S 1), on streets including Wilson Street, Dewdney Trunk Road, Berg Avenue, Rolley Lake Street, Carr Street and Glacier Drive.

The name: "Stave Falls" is both the community name and the name of the falls/power site on the Stave River — BC Hydro's Powerhouse at Stave Falls, built in 1912, was once B.C.'s biggest hydroelectric power source and is now a BC Hydro Visitor Centre and National Historic Site.

The hydro system, from BC Hydro: a three-reservoir, three-generating-station system — water stored in Alouette Lake runs through Alouette Generating Station into Stave Lake, flows through the new powerhouse at Stave Falls into Hayward Lake, and finally through Ruskin Dam and Powerhouse before spilling into the Fraser River three kilometres south. The reservoirs are popular recreation areas; swimming, hiking, biking, fishing and boating are all options, and Hayward Lake in particular gets busy in summer.

Community park project: the City of Mission's engagement site covers a Stave Falls Community Park on Brackley Avenue, designed through a May 2023 community session beside the school, with entryways and park access from Brackley Avenue and the school.

The name and the hydro system: "Stave Falls" is both the community name and the name of the falls/power site on the Stave River. BC Hydro's Powerhouse at Stave Falls was built in 1912, was once B.C.'s biggest hydroelectric power source, and remained in operation until a new powerhouse was built in 2000; the old powerhouse is now a BC Hydro Visitor Centre and National Historic Site. BC Hydro describes a three-reservoir, three-generating-station system — water stored in Alouette Lake runs through Alouette Generating Station into Stave Lake, flows through the new powerhouse at Stave Falls into Hayward Lake, and finally through Ruskin Dam and Powerhouse before spilling into the Fraser River.

Recreation: BC Hydro's Hayward Lake recreation area, near Mission on the Stave River system, is the area's anchor recreation site — the reservoir is an active hydroelectric facility and a popular recreation area, and the nearby Stave Lake boat launch and Ruskin Dam recreation area are also BC Hydro sites; the City of Mission restricts parking on city roads leading to Hayward Lake at busy times.
Nearby areas: Steelhead to the west/southwest, Mission West and Silverdale to the south, Ruskin and Hayward Lake across the Stave River side, and Durieu / the Hatzic Valley to the east.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Stave Falls

items.t: City plans and zoning: Mission's Lougheed Highway Corridor Plan is still being prepared, not adopted; Council endorsed a land use option for it on July 20, 2026. Confirm a lot's plan designation and zoning with the City before counting on density or a second home. The regional district rules that apply in Dewdney-Deroche and Durieu don't apply here.

Secondary suites: in Mission, a suite is a self-contained unit inside a single detached house, on the same title; coach houses and garden cottages are separate detached units. Suites aren't allowed in townhouses or rowhomes, all suites must be registered with the City, new suites need a building permit, and there's an annual suite fee of $63 plus utility fees. Mission has adopted the provincial small-scale housing rules for lots zoned single-family or duplex as of December 7, 2023, subject to eligibility and services, but Stave Falls' rural lots are outside the urban serviced area.

Wells and septic: wells are recorded in the provincial GWELLS database, and onsite sewerage must comply with the Sewerage System Regulation, including the 30 m setback from a well unless professional advice is obtained.

blocks.text: Good to know about Stave Falls condos

items.t: Same mailing look, opposite governance to its neighbours. Dewdney-Deroche and Durieu are unincorporated FVRD ground taxed by the Province under the rural 5% + 5% regime; Stave Falls, which reads just as rural, is inside the City of Mission — City OCP (Bylaw 6405-2026, adopted June 1, 2026), City zoning, and a flat 10% tax penalty after July 2.

A detached second dwelling usually means a rezoning here. City application material for the Stave Falls area shows RU16-to-RU16s rezonings as the worked route to a secondary detached unit on a rural lot outside the Urban Growth Boundary on land designated Rural Residential — the same worked example neighbouring Steelhead owners follow.

items.t: There are no strata townhouses in Stave Falls, so strata rules don't apply here: acreages have no strata, Form B or strata fees, just the title, City rules and registered covenants. City plan — OCP Bylaw 6405-2026, adopted June 1, 2026: Mission's Lougheed Highway Corridor Plan is in preparation, not adopted — Council endorsed Focused Land Use Option #2 on July 20, 2026 — so no corridor-plan adoption is claimed for the Highway 7 approach to this area.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Stave Falls

items.t: SSMUH and suites: the City has adopted the provincial SSMUH legislation for zones previously restricted to single-family or duplex dwellings, subject to eligibility and servicing. Mission suites must be registered with the City and are not permitted in townhouses or rowhomes — there are no townhouses here for that rule to apply to. Listing text from a Nov 2, 2026 search for Stave Falls-area land describes RR7S zoning allowing two dwelling units (suites or carriage homes) on specific Carr Street lots; that is listing text for those lots only, not a zone rule for the sub-area.

Property taxes: Stave Falls is inside the City of Mission, so the City's flat 10% penalty applies. Mission's 2026 taxes were due July 2, 2026, and the City says "A 10% penalty will be added to any current balances outstanding (including unclaimed home owner grants) on July 3, 2026." The rural 5% + 5% schedule applies only to regional district areas outside the City.

Manufactured-home pad rent (MHPTA), where a park home is the purchase instead: pad-rent increases are capped at 2.3% plus a proportional amount for 2026, and 2.2% plus a proportional amount for 2027 — confirmed from the park's own tenancy documents for any specific pad.
Waterfront here is on a working BC Hydro reservoir system (Alouette Lake, Stave Lake, the Stave Falls powerhouse, Hayward Lake, Ruskin Dam and the Fraser River).

Taxes and rebates: property transfer tax is 1% on the first $200,000, 2% from $200,000 to $2 million and 3% above $2 million, plus another 2% on the residential part above $3 million. On a $900,000 acreage house with no exemption, that's $2,000 + $14,000 = $16,000. First-time buyers are exempt on the first $500,000 for homes up to $835,000, with a partial exemption up to $860,000; the newly built home exemption is full up to $1,100,000 and ends at $1,150,000. The GST New Housing Rebate is 36% up to $6,300 (phasing out between $350,000 and $450,000). The Home Buyers' Plan allows $60,000, an FHSA $8,000 a year up to $40,000, and CMHC insurance premiums run 0.6%–4.5%. Manufactured homes on rented pads are often financed differently from fee-simple homes, so check financing first.
Foreclosure note: Mission has no Supreme Court registry.

blocks.text: Good to know about Stave Falls townhomes

items.t: Stave Falls is a city address with a rural market — and the two must not be priced or taxed as each other. Inside the City for OCP, zoning and the flat 10% penalty; acreage, wells, septic and reservoir shoreline for the actual purchase. The neighbouring areas (Dewdney-Deroche, Lake Errock) sit in FVRD electoral areas under the rural tax regime — the boundary between those regimes is a municipal line, not a feel.

The "lake" is a power system. Water stored in Alouette Lake runs through Alouette Generating Station into Stave Lake, through the new Stave Falls powerhouse into Hayward Lake, and through Ruskin Dam into the Fraser River three kilometres south — shoreline use sits inside a working hydro system, which is why dock and moorage claims need BC Hydro and title answers, not listing text.

The old powerhouse outlived its job by a century's turn. Built in 1912, once B.C.'s biggest hydroelectric power source, operating until a new powerhouse replaced it in 2000 — now a Visitor Centre, museum and National Historic Site.

The page's 28 results include land and manufactured homes the board's September 2026 residential splits do not count the same way. Quoting either number as the other is the standing error for this page.
A search for townhouses in this area turns up homes in other places. As far as I know, Stave Falls has no strata homes.

The community park exists as a design, not yet as a confirmed opening. The City's engagement page covers design concepts for a park on Brackley Avenue beside the school, with a survey that closed May 11, 2025.

Hayward Lake is the busy shore, not Stave Lake. Per BC Hydro, the reservoirs offer swimming, hiking, biking, fishing and boating, and Hayward Lake in particular gets busy in summer with swimmers and paddlers — the recreation pitch and the property's actual shoreline are two different checks.

blocks.text: Jared's take on Stave Falls

Around Stave Lake, Hayward Lake and the Stave River, Stave Falls is Mission’s waterfront community, a rural area inside city limits. One thing buyers need to know: the shoreline is a BC Hydro reservoir.
Areas near Stave Falls
The 8 closest neighbourhoods we cover, nearest first. Distances are straight-line between centre points, so the drive is longer.

faq.a: The homes here are acreage houses, vacant acreage lots and manufactured homes in the Wilson Street parks. If you want a Mission condo, look in central Mission, not Stave Falls.
faq.q: Are there any condos in Stave Falls?

faq.a: The City of Mission. Mission's 2026 property taxes were due July 2, 2026, with a flat 10% penalty on balances unpaid on July 3, 2026. The rural rules (pay the Province, with 5% after July 2 and 5% after October 31) don't apply inside the City, even though Stave Falls looks and feels rural.
faq.q: What taxes do I pay on a Stave Falls property — City or Province?

faq.a: The community sits in the Stave Lake / Hayward Lake reservoir system — BC Hydro describes water flowing from Stave Lake through the Stave Falls powerhouse into Hayward Lake, with swimming, boating and fishing on the reservoirs.
faq.q: Is Stave Falls waterfront on Stave Lake?

faq.a: The homes here are acreage houses, vacant acreage lots and manufactured homes in the Wilson Street parks. If you want a Mission condo, look in central Mission, not Stave Falls.
faq.q: Are there any condos in Stave Falls?

faq.a: The City of Mission. Mission's 2026 property taxes were due July 2, 2026, with a flat 10% penalty on balances unpaid on July 3, 2026. The rural rules (pay the Province, with 5% after July 2 and another 5% after October 31) don't apply inside the City, even though Stave Falls looks and feels rural.
faq.q: What taxes do I pay on a Stave Falls property — City or Province?

faq.a: At the Mission community level — not Stave Falls' figures — the detached median sale price was $814,000 and the Condos & Townhomes median was $430,000.
faq.q: What sold in Stave Falls in September 2026?

faq.a: Feed listings repeatedly rely on drilled wells and septic systems; confirm well yield, septic approval and any City service-extension plans for the specific lot rather than assuming municipal services — being inside a city boundary does not mean being on city pipes in rural Mission.
faq.q: Are the acreages on City water and sewer?

faq.a: City planning, zoning and the flat 10% city tax penalty apply here.
faq.q: Is Stave Falls part of Mission — or is it rural FVRD?

faq.a: City of Mission — the Rural Mission Strategy names Stave Falls among the rural communities it covers, inside the City, so City OCP (6405-2026), City zoning (5949-2020) and the flat 10% City tax penalty apply, and the FVRD rural regime (5% + 5%) does not.
faq.q: Is Stave Falls part of Mission, or is it rural FVRD ground?

faq.a: Each parcel is diligenced on title, zone, ALR status, servicing and shoreline tenure.
Confirm well yield, septic approval and any City service-extension plans for the specific lot rather than assuming municipal services.
faq.q: Is the acreage serviced by the City?

faq.a: City bylaws govern, and the tax penalty is Mission's flat 10% city regime, not the rural 5% + 5%.
faq.q: Is Stave Falls even in Mission? It feels like FVRD country.

faq.a: Only if the two halves were legally split, by a two-lot strata plan (in which case read the Form B) or a fee-simple subdivision. I don't know of either for any Stave Falls property.
faq.q: Can I buy half of a Stave Falls house? And is there a strata half duplex here?

faq.a: Yes — Stave Falls is a rural community inside the City of Mission: the City's Rural Mission Strategy names Stave Falls among the rural communities it covers and ties that work to the City's Official Community Plan, so City planning, zoning and tax rules apply here, unlike in unincorporated Dewdney-Deroche to the east.
faq.q: Is Stave Falls part of Mission?

faq.a: BC Hydro's original Stave Falls powerhouse, built in 1912 and once B.C.'s biggest hydroelectric power source; it operated until a new powerhouse replaced it in 2000 and now serves as a BC Hydro Visitor Centre and museum, designated a National Historic Site.
faq.q: What is the Powerhouse at Stave Falls?
